description.narrative:
Sida ger icke-öronmärkt stöd till genomförandet av OHCHR:s landprogram i Uganda under perioden 2021-2023, med ca 10 miljoner SEK per år.
OHCHR:s program i Uganda utgår från dessa fem övergripande mål; 1) stärka rättstatens principer och ansvarsutkrävande angående kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter, 2) verka för jämställdhet och mot diskriminering, 3) främja och försvara demokratiskt utrymme och folkligt deltagande 4) integrera mänskliga rättigheter för hållbar utveckling, 5) stärka engagemanget i MR-mekanismerna.
OHCHR:s unika mandat är att främja och skydda alla mänskliga rättigheter för alla människor, och de är det ledande FN-organet gällande mänskliga rättigheter (MR). I Uganda arbetar OHCHR utifrån sitt nuvarande värdlandsavtal som ger dem mandat att rådge och bistå regeringen, stärka kapaciteten för MR-institutioner och civilsamhällesorganisationer och stödja genomförandet av normer, standards på området och rekommendationer från MR-mekanismer, samt övervaka och rapportera om MR-situationen tillsammans med Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC). De har också en viktig roll i att stärka och säkra en rättighetsbaserad ansats inom FN-familjen och dess olika program.
OHCHR:s landkontor i Kampala har fältkontor i Moroto och i Gulu.

Sida provides core support to the implementation of the OHCHR country program in Uganda during 2021-2023. The annual amount is about 10 million SEK.
OHCHR's country program in Uganda is based on the following five overall goals, or so-called pillars; 1) strengthen the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations, 2) enhance equality and counter discrimination, 3) enhance and protect civic space and public participation, 4) integrate human rights into sustainable development, 5) strengthen engagement with the human rights mechanisms.
The Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR or UN Human Rights) is the lead UN entity on human rights. In Uganda, OHCHR operates according to its current host country agreement that gives them the mandate to advise and assist the government on formulation and implementation of policies and programs relating to human rights, strengthen the capacity of national human rights institutions and CSOs, support implementation of international HR norms and standards and recommendations from HR mechanisms, and monitor the human rights situation in the country, in partnership with the Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC).

Most of the activities of the OHCHR office in Uganda concerns capacity building, technical assistance, trainings, workshops and dialogue meetings etc. This is explained by OHCHRs aim at advocacy and participation as well as building national capacity, be it with duty bearers, rights holders and their intermediaries. Despite the difficulties to measure the impact of such activities, six key achievements are highlighted during the agreement period (2021-2023), with the majority taking place in 2021 and 2022 for obvious reasons. These are:
• In 2022, OHCHR supported the Uganda Human Right Commission (UHRC) to secure the release of over 1800 people arbitrarily detained by security forces. The vast majority had been arrested and detained in the context of the ongoing forcible disarmament operation in Karamoja. OHCHR contributed to increased accountability for human rights violations by supporting the Karamoja Regional Protection Meetings, bringing together the army, police, prison service, local Government officials, the judiciary, Civil Society Organisations and UN agencies to address human rights issues in Karamoja.
• OHCHR increased the awareness, knowledge and application of the Prevention and Prohibition of Torture Act, 2012 and the Human Rights Enforcement Act, 2019 (HREA) among judges, lawyers and police officers, resulting in judges increasingly invoking the HREA in judicial decision-making.
• OHCHR supported the development and dissemination of the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights adopted in 2021, making Uganda only the second country in Africa to adopt one.
• Support the development and launch of an info graphic booklet on albinism entitled Just Like You! to be used as an advocacy tool to combat stigma and discrimination against members of the albinism community by clarifying myths and stereotypes about albinism launched in early 2023.
• In 2022, OHCHR contributed to the reduction of the backlog of treaty body reports by supporting the MGLSD and MoFA to develop a submit a State report to the Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and combined State reports to the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights.
• OHCHR updated the search engine/human rights database, initially developed in 2016, to track Uganda's progress towards implementation of human rights recommendations made by the UN, African Union and the UHRC. The database improved the Government analysis and reporting to the UN and AU. It is accessible to the public and remains a useful advocacy tool for engaging with the Government on human rights issues.
Despite its quite limited mandate in Uganda and closure of the office, the OHCHR has still managed to achieved a few activities/results in 2023. For 2023, the activity period mainly covered January - February and thus only a few results under goal one and two are highlighted.
************************************************************ Below are some examples of key results achieved in 2023 outlined in the report:
Goal 1: Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations
Result 1. Laws, policies and practices are in line with international human rights obligations and increasingly address, prevent and reduce human rights violations in the context of law enforcement and justice systems.
- In January and February 2023, OHCHR delivered a number of training sessions, jointly with the UHRC, for journalists, media professionals and law enforcement agencies under the Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda (SEPU) project, which at the time had been extended until the end of March 2023. In the course of the trainings, OHCHR had frank exchanges about the challenges faced by journalists, law enforcement officers in the course of their work. Journalists regarding safety concerns, pressures from security forces and online harassment.
Result 2. Strengthened national mechanisms to provide redress to victims and ensure accountability for human rights violations, including economic and social rights.
- OHCHR alongside UHRC participated in a joint human rights monitoring mission in Kaabong, Karenga and Kotido districts from 27 February - 3 March 2023. This monitoring mission intended to verify and investigate the allegations of human rights violations reported in north Karamoja during the period of quarter four of 2022 and January and February of 2023. It also aimed at raising human rights issues and concerns to be identified with responsible state institutions. Some of the achievements of the mission included the completion of investigation of seven complaints which had been referred to the UHRC, six new complaints registered by UHRC, a meeting with Regional Police Commander and Regional Criminal Investigation Directorate officer of UPF in Kidepo to raise concerns over the alleged human rights violations of police officers at the Central Police Station in Kaabong district.
Goal 2: Enhancing equality and countering discrimination
Result 1. Laws, policies and practices more effectively combat discrimination in all its forms
- Since the Anti-Homosexuality Bill (AHA) was tabled before Parliament in March 2023, OHCHR closely monitored the legislative process and engaged in sustained advocacy against its promulgation into law.
- Under the leadership of OHCHR HQ and country office, the UN System made a submission to the Parliament of the Republic of Uganda on the AHA as part of the UN continuous commitment to support Ugandas efforts to meet its international human rights obligations and to advance sustainable development and enhance the quality of life of all persons in the country (13 March 2023). Specifically, OHCHR highlighted key areas of the law that are not compatible with Uganda's international human rights obligations and requested the Parliament to review, repeal and establish a moratorium on the application of all Laws that criminalize same sex conduct between consenting adults Laws that criminalize transgender people on the basis of their gender expression other laws used to arrest, punish or discriminate against people on the basis of their sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression.
- OHCHR monitored the implementation of the AHA and referred approximately 30 victims to organisations and agencies that are currently providing protection measures, medical and financial support to them.
- OHCHR supported the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (MGLSD) towards the validation of a National Affirmative Action Program for Indigenous Peoples (NAAPIP) in Mukono, Uganda. OHCHR provided financial, logistical and administrative, while MGLSD was responsible for implementing and mobilizing all participants and interpreters (25 May 2023).
Result 2. Women and girls, people with disabilities, people living with HIV/AIDS, people with albinism, indigenous people and LGBTI people are better able to attain equal human rights
- OHCHR supported the MGLSD to print the National Action Plan for Person with Albinism and the National Policy for Person with Disabilities in braille formats, for MGLSD, National Counsel for Persons with Disabilities (NCPD), Members of Parliament including the representatives of persons with disabilities (PWDs), Committee for Gender, Labor and Social Development, Committee on Human Rights and Committee on Equal Opportunities (27 April 2023).
- OHCHR supported the NCPD to launch and disseminate the 2020-2021 National Disability Status Report in Kampala. Participants comprised of Members of Parliament including the representatives of persons with disabilities, Committee for Gender, labor and Social Development, Committee on Human Rights and Committee on Equal Opportunities, MDAs, UHRC and UN agencies (UN Women, UNICEF, UNDP, UNFPA), District Councils for disability, organizations of People With Disabilities, and development partners (29 March 2023).
- OHCHR, UHRC and United Organization for Batwa Development in Uganda (UOBDU) conducted one-day community Barazza for human rights training in three Sub-Counties (Bukimbiri, Murora, and Busanza within Kisoro District), from 27 February to 1 March 2023.
************************************************************ Below are some examples of key results achieved in 2022:
Goal 1. Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations
- OHCHR with UHRC have secured the release of at a total of 1805 detainees in Karamoja, Kampala and Gulu as follows 1589 detainees in Karamoja, 186 in Kampala and 30 in Gulu.
- OHCHR successfully advocated for improved detention conditions in places of military and civilian detention in Karamoja and the northern region.
- OHCHR contributed to increased awareness, knowledge and application of the Prevention and Prohibition of Torture Act, 2012 (PPTA) and Human Rights Enforcement Act, 2019 (HREA) among judges, lawyers and police officers, resulting in Judges increasingly invoke the HREA in judicial decision-making.
- OHCHR provided technical support for UHRCs memorandum to the Judiciary highlighting areas for human rights compliance within the Bail Guidelines which resulted in some of the human rights concerns being addressed by removing provisions.
- OHCHR contributed to reviving and maintaining high on the agenda the fight against death penalty by supporting the UHRC and UPS to commemorate the World Day against the Death Penalty. This resulted into increased awareness on the human rights implications of the death penalty and renewed commitment of development stakeholders to advocate for the abolition of the death penalty in Uganda.
- OHCHR organised four regional human rights working group protection meetings in Lango and Acholi sub-regions and improved coordination between HRDs, civil society organisations, law enforcement and local government officials for more effective follow-up of alleged human rights violations.
Goal 2. Enhancing equality and countering discrimination
- OHCHR supported and reinforced UN Women and the entire UNCTs technical capacities by developing a human rights analysis of the Marriage Bill to inform UN Agencies advocacy on human rights concerns in the Bill.
- OHCHR increased awareness of the rights of people with albinism through launching Just Like You! Addressing Myths and Misconceptions on Albinism.
- OHCHR strengthened duty bearers sense of human rights responsibility and obligation by supporting the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development to launch and distribute 180 copies of the National Action Plan for Persons with Albinism.
- OHCHR reinforced awareness on State and collective responsibility of society to protect women's rights by supporting UHRC to organise a High Level National Symposium on SGBV OHCHR contributed to a greater inclusivity in line with the Leave No One Behind principle by producing and distributing 1000 copies of the Ugandan Bill of Rights in the Lusoga language.
Goal 3. Enhancing and protecting civic space and peoples participation
- OHCHR built the capacity of 55 CSO representatives, including 26 women and 29 men, to monitor and document human rights violations and abuses and to record them in the human rights database. The database analysis has been used as an advocacy tool in CSOs advocacy with local authorities.
- OHCHR built the capacity of 51 journalists, including 25 women and 26 men to better incorporate human rights and gender in their reporting. OHCHR has observed improved human rights and gender sensitive reporting by journalists.
- OHCHR contributed to reduce impunity for human rights violations in Karamoja by conducting at least 30 monitoring activities that investigated individual complaints of human rights violations resulting in at least 73 new complaints being lodged with the UHRC related to the ongoing disarmament operations in Karamoja subregion.
- OHCHR contributed to increased accountability for human rights violations by supporting the organization of four Karamoja Regional Protection Meetings held to address human rights violations and abuses in Karamoja.
- OHCHR built the capacity of the UHRC to conduct human rights monitoring missions, including on business and human rights and the situation of the Benet Indigenous People in the Mount Elgon region.
- OHCHR contributed to increase the institutional capacities and effectiveness of the UHRC by supporting technically and financially the institution to produce, print and release its 24th annual report on the State of Human Rights in Uganda in 2021 that was submitted to Parliament.
Goal 4. Integrating human rights in sustainable development
- OHCHR contributed to a change of paradigm and increased awareness of government actors, business community and rights holders in the area of business and human rights by supporting the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development to popularize and implement the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights at the national and regional level.
- OHCHR built the skills and knowledge of 40 UHRC staff on the SDGs and monitoring business and human rights to inform their monitoring activities.
- OHCHR built the capacities of the Ministry of Health to mainstream HRBA into health services in refugee hosting districts in West Nile and South western Uganda.
Goal 5. Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms' outcomes
- OHCHR contributed to the reduction of the backlog of human rights reports to international mechanisms by supporting the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to develop and submit two overdue human rights reports: a State report to the Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and combined State reports to the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights (ACHPR). The report to the ICPRD was submitted to Geneva on 6 February 2023 and the ACHPR report to the AU Commission on 19 November 2022.
- OHCHR contributed to improving the level of follow-up and implementation of recommendations emanating from human rights mechanisms by training representatives of Government ministries, departments and agencies on tracking/coordinating implementation of human rights recommendations, including populating through the database for MDAs and IMCHR.
Integrating human rights and gender into United Nation Country Team (UNCT) operations.
The OHCHR office has also played an important role in integrating human rights and gender into the different UN entities in Uganda. Examples of achievements within this area are:
- OHCHR increased UNCTs knowledge and awareness of human rights issues through ensuring a standing agenda item at UNCT meetings on human rights, gender and disability inclusion.
- OHCHR contributed to the development of the System Wide Action Plan (SWAP) Gender Scorecard. OHCHR built the capacity of UN staff on Gender, Human Rights, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse in Gulu, Fort Portal and Lira.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
